turns.prompt_text: How do I use this bottle jack Attached 1 file. - 827c7993-6955-4a91-854b-6e4460fc497f
turns.response_html:
That Pittsburgh 12-ton bottle jack is a beast, but it’s only as safe as the person operating it. Since it’s a hydraulic tool, the "magic" happens through fluid pressure, and there’s a specific sequence you need to follow to make sure it lifts—and stays—where you want it.

Here is the quick-start guide to using it:

1. Position and Prep

  • Surface: Only use the jack on a hard, level surface (like concrete). Using it on the carpet (like in the photo) or dirt is dangerous because it can tilt or sink.
  • Park: If you're lifting a vehicle, put it in Park, engage the emergency brake, and chock the wheels on the opposite end.

2. Close the Release Valve

  • Look at the base of the jack. There is a small screw/valve (usually near where the handle inserts).
  • Use the notched end of your handle to turn this valve clockwise until it is snug. If this isn't closed, the jack won't rise when you pump.

3. Place the Jack

  • Slide the jack under the vehicle’s designated jacking point (check your owner's manual; usually a frame rail or a reinforced metal area).
  • Pro Tip: You can unscrew the textured "saddle" (the top red part) by hand to extend it upward before you start pumping. This saves you a lot of manual pumping time.

4. Lift

  • Insert the handle into the handle sleeve and pump up and down with full strokes.
  • Once the saddle makes contact, ensure it is centered and stable. Continue pumping until you reach your desired height.

5. Secure with Jack Stands (Critical)

  • Never work under a vehicle supported only by a jack. Hydraulic seals can fail.
  • Once lifted, slide a jack stand under a secure part of the frame and slowly lower the jack until the weight is resting on the stand.

How to Lower It

When you're done, pump the jack slightly to clear the jack stands, remove the stands, and then very slowly turn the release valve counter-clockwise. The weight of the vehicle will push the fluid back into the reservoir and the jack will retract.

Safety Note: Since that's a "Low Profile" model, it's great for getting under lower vehicles, but 12 tons is a massive amount of pressure. Always keep your hands and feet clear of the "pinch zone" while lowering.
